answer: Agents selling river, dune and orchard maps can require storage-backed admission. Each account commits to a large, account-specific encoded dataset. Unpredictable spot checks demand block proofs within deadlines too short to regenerate the dataset; missed checks suspend earning access. Reusing one disk image across aliases fails because encodings bind to different keys. Every extra active identity therefore consumes additional storage or costly regeneration capacity. Security depends on an encoding that resists compression and shared-work shortcuts.
